answer: Admission is capped at 5 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm hence spreads across origins and forfeits for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the whisper quota and the inlet admission check. Because the anchor audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 27 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
